messages:
incident-bot: [P1] runtime OOM detected in runtime-prod-us-east-1 (gpu-pool-12). Affected: inference-api. Autoscaler triggered, paging events increasing. Pager: @Anna (oncall).

Anna (oncall): I'm on it — ack. Initial check: spikes in GPU paging and a few 502s to customers. ETA 5m to collect traces.

Jess (cs): flagging CS: small set of customers (acct ids sent via DM) report intermittent 502s, most retries succeeded. Notified. :frowning:

Sam (runtime): hypothesis: kv-cache fragmentation + sudden large batch traffic (batch=16) pushed some pods over alloc threshold -> allocator OOM -> paging. Requesting GPU mem + allocator logs from affected hosts.

Dalia (infra): pulling metrics now. Prometheus queries I ran: 
```
sum(gpu_mem_used_bytes{pool="gpu-pool-12"}) by (instance)
// shows 95%+ on instance i-0a1b2c3d4e5f
avg_over_time(gpu_paging_events_total[5m])
```
Samples: i-0a1b2c3d4e5f: mem_used 15.8GB/16GB, paging spikes ~120/s. Other nodes at 60-70% used.

Mike (sre): can we temporarily reduce incoming batch size for inference-api to 8 and mark node i-0a1b2c3d4e5f as drained? That should stop new large allocations. Also consider evicting long-lived KV entries to free up contiguous memory.

Anna (oncall): doing quick mitigation: toggling feature-flag to cap batch_size=8 for prod routes now. Command: 
```
curl -X POST "https://config.redwood/api/flags" -d '{"inference.batch_max":8}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```
Rolling to 20% canary -> 100% in 3m if stable.

Anna (oncall): also issuing drain on i-0a1b2c3d4e5f: `kubectl cordon i-0a1b2c3d4e5f && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data i-0a1b2c3d4e5f`

Sam (runtime): saw allocator error in logs from that host: 
```
2026-03-17T18:34:12Z runtime: alloc failed: requested=1288490188 (1.2GB) total_free=1073741824 (1.0GB)
runtime: kvcache fragmentation: largest_free_contiguous=256MB
```
Suggest lowering kvcache.max_mem_pct on that pod and enable kvcache.eviction_aggressiveness=high for hot shards.

Dalia (infra): grabbing full allocator dump + gpu slab stats. Attaching short snippet: 
```
GPU0 slab: free_chunks=12 largest=256MB fragmented=62%
KVCache shards: shard-17 mem=3.1GB, entries=124k, avg_entry=25KB
```
I'll upload the full dump to /private/incidents/3330004444/dumps shortly.

Jess (cs): drafting a customer note: "We observed transient errors due to internal memory pressure; mitigation applied, error rate returning to baseline. We're investigating root cause and will follow up."

Anna (oncall): send now as an interim update. Include "limited window, small % of requests affected, retries succeeded". I'll update once we have timeline.

Mike (sre): building timeline request: can we each paste earliest evidence times and last observed impacts. I'll consolidate. My entries: paging spike start 2026-03-17T18:33:40Z, autoscaler X attempts at 18:34:05Z, first 502 spike at 18:34:10Z.

Sam (runtime): adding: first allocator OOM trace 18:34:12Z on i-0a1b2c3d4e5f, repeated until 18:35:08Z. Batch queue saw transient backlog 18:33:50-18:36:00Z.

Dalia (infra): metrics: GPU paging peak 18:34:00-18:35:30Z, kernel page reclaim activity high. Network retransmits low, so likely local memory problem.

Anna (oncall): mitigation results: canary batch cap at 20% -> latency stable, rolling to 100% at 18:36:00Z. Drained node done at 18:37:20Z. Error rate back to baseline by 18:38:10Z.

Sam (runtime): preliminary root cause candidates: 1) KV cache fragmentation from long-lived large entries + per-request large KV pulls; 2) temporary shift in traffic pattern (spike of large multi-turn sessions) causing unusually large contiguous alloc requests; 3) possible allocator regression in latest runtime (re: recent slab change).

Mike (sre): next actions (short):
- Collect full allocator dumps/kv shard maps (Dalia)
- Reproduce in staging with high batch loads and long sessions (Sam)
- Temporary config: kvcache.max_mem_pct=0.65 and eviction_aggressiveness=high rollout to canary (Anna/Sam)
- Postmortem timeline + customer impact (Anna/Jess)

Anna (oncall): assigning owner for RCA writeup: @Sam takes lead, @Dalia supplies infra dumps, @Mike reviews timeline, @Jess handles comms. I'll hand off to Sam in 30m for deep dive.

Jess (cs): sent interim customer update at 18:40Z. Notified accounts and support channels.

Sam (runtime): will run a targeted reproducibility test now: reproduce traffic shape with batch=16, long session retention, monitor fragmentation and largest_free_contiguous. Will post run logs to the dump path.

Anna (oncall): handing off active ticket to @Sam (runtime) for RCA. Oncall remains reachable for escalation. Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. :white_check_mark:

Mike (sre): small note: consider adding an alarm for contiguous_free_bytes < threshold per GPU to catch fragmentation early rather than just utilization.

Dalia (infra): uploaded dumps: /private/incidents/3330004444/{alloc-dump-18_34.tar.gz,kvshard-map.json,gpu-slab-stats.txt}.

Sam (runtime): received artifacts. I'll start the RCA doc and timeline; will include hypothesis tests and propose a runtime patch if allocator regression is found.

Anna (oncall): thanks team. I'll tag this thread for the postmortem and move to the incidents tracker. Handoff complete."
